tier_reason: No benchmark_url and no speed number anywhere: the README, repo page, releases notes (v0.0.11 to v1.3.3) and issue search for 'performance' carry none, and mfabbri77/VGCPU-Benchmark lists a plutovg backend (labelled 0.0.4) beside Cairo 1.18.2, Skia m124 and Blend2D but commits no results (perf/ holds only perf_suite_scenes.txt; docs/ has no reports). With no numbers it cannot rise above D.

corrections.caveats: No speed number in the README, repo page, release notes, the issue tracker (a 'performance' search returns only #65 and #43, neither about speed), the LunaSVG README, or WebSearch. Lead: run mfabbri77/VGCPU-Benchmark (0 stars, MIT, last commit 2026-08-31, has a report generator and pre-baked versus full-lifecycle modes, but commits no results; perf/ holds only a scene list) to obtain numbers against Cairo, Skia and Blend2D; its README labels the plutovg backend version 0.0.4, older than the current v1.3.3. Indirect only: the listed LunaSVG entry (which renders through plutovg) has a third-party pipeline benchmark against cairosvg and resvg-py (pillow-lunasvg benchmarks/results.md), but it times Python parse, render and PNG encode, gives no render-only figure for Cairo, and so is not a plutovg-versus-Cairo rasteriser comparison. Usability mixed: the project licence is MIT, but the vendored FreeType-derived files source/plutovg-ft-raster.c (ftgrays), plutovg-ft-stroker.c and plutovg-ft-math.c carry the FreeType Project License header (source/FTL.TXT is included; permissive with an attribution/credits requirement, not OSI-approved).

notes: Metadata matches the record (MIT, 527 stars, 69 forks, not a fork, not archived, last commit 2026-07-16, v1.3.3 latest release dated May 18). Kept rather than rejected as not-notable: it is the rasteriser behind the already-listed LunaSVG and PlutoSVG and is a distinct library, not a wrapper or port, so it is not a duplicate. VGCPU-Benchmark remains the route to real numbers.
